The 09:00 default does NOT reach the prompt (humanFactsBlock pushes p.value only, never p.due) — I checked, because a fabricated appointment time spoken to a customer would have been a REDEVELOP.

Zero WhatsApp sends anywhere in the cycle (CLAUDE.md §8 + user-model Rule 5), held by GUPSHUP_* forced empty AND a fetch-layer spy. No secret touched, no data deletion, no spend. props is deliberately absent from upsertContact's ON CONFLICT clause so no unrelated event can null a typed fact — AC-5 verified it end to end with a re-hydrate. Provenance carried by SHAPE (filled square / dashed circle / dashed outline) so it survives greyscale and colour-blindness, all six marks on one vertical axis so provenance is scannable before a single label is read, per-field commit (HubSpot's idiom, explicitly not Salesforce's whole-form mode), gaps collected in ONE dedicated panel exactly as HubSpot's data-quality section does rather than scattered asterisks, and the mark never appears without its word so a row lifted out of context still says «سجّلها عبدالعزيز». Anti-AI-aesthetics: no gradient, no generic card stack, no decorative iconography; every colour is spent on meaning. grill.verdict: FINDINGS — the root of M1/M2; and a large earned credit
grill.evidence: CREDIT: the BR-1 invariant is STRUCTURAL, not behavioural — one door (tracker.writeProp), deeply Readonly props so `c.props.note = …` is a tsc error outside the module, props kept out of upsertContact's SQL, a gate that fails if any other module writes props, DB-before-memory so a refused ledger write cannot leave a phantom value, and decideProp pure and exported so the guard is testable without Postgres. This is the right shape and it is why nothing in this diff can rot back. FINDING (the root cause of both musts): `nextStep.due` is a SECOND representation of an appointment that `c.scheduledAt`/`c.scheduledSaid` already own, with no reconciliation in either direction. Rule 8 says build the PLACE the data lives; this built a second place. Every symptom below follows from that one decision.

58 distinct onclick handlers lifted from the shipped bundle, every one resolves to a definition — zero dead buttons. Zero TODO/FIXME/lorem/placeholder/«قريبًا» in the src diff. No invented number anywhere on the record: contextScore (a 0-100 score over fields we happen to hold, which read FULL on a customer whose only sentence was «ماني مهتم») is deleted, the 6-node rail is deleted AND its renderer removed so no future edit can re-call it, and check-outcomes.mjs bans the identifier. The tests are not vacuous: check-props lifts the emitted bundle and RUNS it — I reused that harness myself and it exercises real branches. The empty-state copy is specific and useful («لا ملاحظات. اكتب ما لا يظهر في المحادثة.»), not filler.

change_orders.order: Render the WHEN. A human-written nextStep date is stored and displayed NOWHERE. Measured, not read: I lifted vFactsPanel out of the shipped bundle and rendered a fact-state nextStep carrying due=25 Aug 2026 — the row prints «زيارة الفرع الرئيسي · سجّلها عبدالعزيز · ١٢ أغسطس» and the 25th does not appear; the same fixture with source:'agent' prints «قراءتنا: ٢٥ أغسطس ٠٩:٠٠ · لم تُؤكَّد بعد». So the machine's GUESS at the date is shown and the human's CONFIRMED date is hidden — exactly backwards from the panel's thesis. Root cause: dashboard.ts:2273, the `parsed` line is gated on `s4.state === 'reading'`, and it is the only consumer of `due`. Fix: render the date in the fact state too, as its own signed line («الموعد: الثلاثاء ٢٥ أغسطس · سجّله عبدالعزيز»). CRITICAL CONSTRAINT: render the DAY only for a human-set date. dayToMs stores 09:00 Riyadh for a bare date, and printing «٠٩:٠٠» back would be a fabricated fact wearing a human signature — the exact class this cycle spent three commits killing. Store the time or don't, but never display a time no human typed.

«أكّد» must not silently narrow the value it confirms. Measured, not read: I lifted propPost out of the shipped bundle and ran the confirm path with document.getElementById returning null — which is what a confirm IS, since no editor is open — and the request body is {"props":{"nextStep":"زيارة الفرع"}}. The due is absent, so decideProp builds a fresh prop with no `due` and the agent's parsed date is DROPPED by the act of confirming it. The most valuable action in the product is lossy, and it loses precisely the datum his third question asks for. Fix at the source, not at the call site: propConfirm should carry the whole prop forward (value AND due AND anything a later property gains), or propPost should default `due` to the stored value rather than to undefined when no date control is on screen — so a seventh field added next quarter cannot re-open this hole.

One appointment, one place — then teach it to every surface that speaks about it. M1 and M2 are symptoms; the cause is that `props.nextStep.due` is a second store for a thing `c.scheduledAt`/`c.scheduledSaid` already own, with no reconciliation. Consequences, all live today: (a) قائمة الصباح — the screen whose own source comment quotes «who are interested, who are not, and if interested, when are we going to schedule them» — reads c.scheduledAt only, so an operator who types the real appointment into ملف العميل still sees «قراءتنا …» or «لم نقرأ تاريخًا» on his morning list; (b) the status strip at dashboard.ts:2420 appends «· لم تُؤكَّد بعد» to c.scheduledAt unconditionally, so a confirmed appointment reads as unconfirmed forever. Fix: a human write to nextStep.due updates the appointment the rest of the portal reads, and the «لم تُؤكَّد بعد» sentence gains a confirmed form. Rule 6's fifth corollary and Rule 8's corollary, together: when a fix invents a state («مؤكَّد»), the FIRST place to carry it is the shared reader — and grep the OLD accessor (c.scheduledAt) call sites before calling the class closed. There are exactly three (2273, 2420, 1678); read all three out loud in the report.

Re-run the delivery gate at the commit that ships. .orbit/qa/delivery-evidence.json is bound to f54835c; 2c88b56 is what is deployed, and delivery-quality-gate.py --commit 2c88b56 returns passed:false. The evidence at f54835c is genuinely strong — this is not a paperwork complaint. It is that the 44 lines nobody gated are where both musts above live, which is the argument for the gate stated better than any policy could state it. After M1-M3, produce evidence at the new commit including a scenario that would go RED on M1 (render a fact-state nextStep with a due and assert the day appears) and one that would go RED on M2 (confirm a dated reading and assert the due survives the round trip). Per Rule 7: before submitting them, revert the fix and check the tests actually fail.

Build the confirmation-rate dividend, or say out loud that it is deferred and why. discovery.md §3 sold it as the surprise («the agent's interest reading is confirmed X% of the time — the only thing that makes an 18,000-contact blast trustworthy»), requirements §2 justified the whole `prior` field by it, and AC-4 verified `prior` is written. The ingredient is in the ledger and the dish is unbuilt. One honest ratio over non-test contacts, with its denominator named and «لا بيانات كافية بعد» below a floor, is a day's work and it is the number that makes 18,000 sends defensible.

Make «ناقص ٥» count what the eye counts. The chip says five above six visibly dashed rows because سبب الاستبعاد is shown but deliberately not counted. He validates numbers against his own lived experience within seconds (R48/R49). Either count six, or name the denominator in the chip («٥ من ٥ حقول أساسية») so the number and the screen agree.

Decide what مرحلة البيع is FOR. On live data stage_reason is empty, so the third row of the status strip is permanently a grey chip plus «قراءة المساعد — بلا اقتباس يسندها بعد». The honest fallback is correct and I credit it — but Rule 4 says a status widget that cannot justify itself does not ship, and this one has never justified itself on real data. Either make refreshInsights populate stage_reason with the quote that produced the stage, or drop the row until it can. A permanent «I have a reading but no reason» is the decorative-inference shape he rejected at R27.

Finish design-plan §5's deletion in the state it missed. In the `ins.learning` branch the AI card still renders toneBadge over ins.product_interest — the third, unsourced rendering of interest that §5 deleted from the non-learning branch. Rule 6's second corollary: enumerate STATES, not just screens.

Widen what user-events.jsonl captures. «yes CRM like hubspot please redesign it and add better indicators for users to enrich them» spawned a five-artifact cycle and three commits, and it is not in the event log — the newest entry is U116. A sentence that redirects the product is durable by definition, whether or not it sounds like a rule. I have recorded it in user-model.md this round; the capture rule should not have needed me to.

waived_shoulds.item: مرحلة البيع is read-only where Wati/Kommo make stage a dropdown (raised by the watchdog).
waived_shoulds.waiver: Not a finding, and I want the reasoning on the record so it is not re-litigated. In HubSpot the editable rail property is LIFECYCLE STAGE — and Massar has that: it is الفرز, set by the four outcome buttons, and it drives قائمة الصباح. مرحلة البيع here is a model INFERENCE about conversation progress, and making an inference editable would either overwrite itself on the next insights run or become a seventh property nobody asked for. Read-only is right. S3 is about whether it earns its place at all, which is the better question.

waived_shoulds.waiver: Not this cycle's job — his ask was scoped to «the ui inside client page», and قائمة الصباح already groups every contact by outcome with the customer's own words for the time.
